doc.title: Lou Pallo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2007

title: Recording with the Four Seasons
summary: Roles of several guitarists on Four Seasons records, listening in stereo, and commercials made with Frankie Valli.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: So what is the, sort of the assignment of roles between those two or three guitar players? What is one person doing and the other person doing?

Oh okay, I’ve done that too, for the Four Seasons. Again that’s sort of like a rock group, we call that rock. We’ve had, I think there were four guitar players on that if I recall. Vinnie Bell. You’ve heard of Vinnie Bell I think? Vinnie was on it. There was someone, a young boy who was about 18 playing acoustic and Tommy DeVito, he was one of the Four Seasons. There was four guitarists. My part was just to play, not rhythm like big band style, just arpeggio type rhythms every — maybe in a measure you’d have the arpeggio type thing, you’d just strum down, then you would strum down, and then maybe play two beats here, one beat here. That they could write at that time. And it just gave color. Because you had so many other guitar players. And I think Vinnie played the same thing but not the same arpeggio in the same spot and the way it came together, we did quite a few of their records and I’m trying to remember, like “Tell it to the Rain,” “I’ve Got You Under My Skin,” and all those. We were on those, and a bunch of other ones.
Was someone assigned to the, just the two and four?
No they really didn’t do it on that. Well just on the rock part if — yeah, what we used to call the chicks.
You recall that. Now you play piano?

Well I’m a fan of that music and I like to listen to what the rhythm section is doing. And what’s neat sometimes on those old — in fact some of the Four Seasons records — if you have stereo, the way they mixed them you can pan it all the way to one side or the other
and they used to put all the vocals on one side and the band is on the other. So you can really hone in on —
Oh. I’ll have to try that on some of the records I have.
Yeah. It doesn’t work for everything and in some of the remixes they didn’t do that. But I’m talking about sometimes if you’re listening to the oldies station in the car you know, try it.
Oh you can do that there, okay.
Sometimes you can say oh, that’s neat.

Because we did, if I recall on the Four Seasons recordings Frankie didn’t even sing, Frankie Valli of course, and they didn’t do their background, but they did put it on later on. He might have done a scratch track of the vocal if I recall that, he did that. And we did a lot of commercials too. In those days all the rock & roll groups and groups were doing commercials for different stations. Like, “Hi this is Frankie Valli for KTLM in Oklahoma City” and we would be playing in the background and then mix those up. We did a lot of those.
